summary: An overview article, dated October 12, 2023, on the fundamentals of aging and the local health and wellness resources available to seniors and caregivers. It covers the biology of aging, nutrition, physical activity, mental health, preventative care, social engagement, adapting living needs, and financial planning. Each section pairs expert quotes with named local programs and events.
one_line: Overview of aging fundamentals and local community programs for seniors covering biology, diet, exercise, mental health, prevention, social life, home safety, and finances.
key_facts: The global population aged 65 and over is expected to reach 1.5 billion by 2050.
Telomeres, protective caps on chromosome ends, shorten with each cell division, leading to cellular aging and reduced ability to regenerate and repair.
Dr. Elizabeth Faust, a geriatrician, said on September 15, 2023 that aging is about the intricate biological changes our bodies undergo, not merely years lived.
Seniors need fewer calories but the same or higher levels of nutrients as metabolism slows, and thirst sensation diminishes with age, raising dehydration risk.
The Fresh Fare Project, launched November 1, 2023, offers nutrient-rich meal plans and healthy-eating education for the elderly.
The Silver Strides walking club was inaugurated on September 30, 2023 to encourage sociability and gentle cardiovascular exercise.
The Mind Matters program, launched September 25, 2023, offers memory-enhancing games, workshops, and social engagements.
The Healthy Horizons screenings program started October 2, 2023, providing preventative care through health fairs and mobile clinics regardless of mobility or income.
Dr. Emily Stanton said on September 18, 2023 that 'Prevention is preferable to treatment, especially in our golden years.'
Recommended senior screenings include blood pressure checks, cancer screenings, bone density tests, and eye exams.
The Golden Years Festival launched September 28, 2023, combining music, art, and cultural activities for the elderly.
The Senior Home Safety program, rolled out October 15, 2023, provides assessments and grants for home modifications.
Martin Clarke held a free estate planning seminar for the elderly on October 1, 2023.
Loneliness and social isolation increase the risk of mortality and mental health issues in seniors.
